statement: You are given an integer array nums and an integer m.
Split nums into exactly m non-empty subarrays, each a contiguous piece of the array. Each split has a largest subarray sum; make that largest sum as small as possible.

Return the minimised largest sum. The answer lies between max(nums) and the sum of nums. For a candidate cap, cutting greedily whenever the running sum would pass it gives the fewest pieces possible, so binary search for the smallest cap that needs at most m pieces.

examples.explanation: Splitting into [7, 2, 5] and [10, 8] gives sums 14 and 18. No split into two pieces keeps both sums below 18.
[1, 2, 3], [4], [5] has largest sum 6. A cap of 5 would force four pieces: [1, 2], [3], [4], [5].
